content.content:
**Neon plans at a glance**

| Plan | Monthly price | Included storage | History (restore window) | Compute |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **Free** | $0, permanent | 1 GB Postgres per project, 20 GB total; 5 GB Object Storage per project | 6 hours (1 GB limit); no instant restore | 100 CU-hours per project; autoscales up to 2 CU |
| **Launch** | Pay for usage, no monthly minimum | Unlimited Postgres at $0.35/GB-month | Up to 7 days; instant restore at $0.20/GB-month | $0.106 per CU-hour; autoscales up to 16 CU |
| **Scale** | Pay for usage, no monthly minimum | Unlimited Postgres at $0.35/GB-month | Up to 30 days; instant restore at $0.20/GB-month | $0.222 per CU-hour; autoscales up to 16 CU, or fixed sizes up to 56 CU |

**Compute and CU:** A CU (Compute Unit) is roughly 4 GB of RAM plus CPU and SSD, so your reading of 1 CU ≈ 4 GB RAM is correct. Compute is billed as CU-hours (compute size × hours running). Suspended compute costs nothing.

**Backup retention:** The page doesn't use the term "backup retention." The closest details are:
- **Snapshots:** Free allows 1 manual snapshot per project. Launch and Scale allow 100 manual snapshots, plus scheduled snapshots at $0.09/GB-month.
- **History window:** This is the restore window described above.

For exact backup retention policies, check the [Plans](https://neon.com/docs/introduction/plans.md) page.

content.content:
**Plan costs**
- **Free:** $0/month, with $1 of free credit per month.
- **Hobby:** $5/month, including $5 of resource usage.
- **Pro:** $20/month, including $20 of resource usage.
- **Enterprise:** Custom pricing.

**Resource pricing (usage beyond included amounts)**
- **RAM:** $10 per GB per month.
- **CPU:** $20 per vCPU per month.
- **Volume storage:** $0.15 per GB per month.
- **Network egress:** $0.05 per GB.
- **Builds:** Free. Railway doesn't charge for build CPU, memory, or image storage.

Included usage resets each billing cycle and doesn't carry over. You pay only the amount by which usage exceeds it.

**Free tier and trial**
- New Trial accounts get a one-time $5 credit. Railway uses that credit before any purchased credits.
- Trial users can't buy credits unless they upgrade to Hobby.

**Backups and data retention**
The page doesn't describe backups directly. It covers two related policies:
- **Image retention (for rollbacks):** Free/Trial keeps removed deployment images for 24 hours, Hobby for 72 hours, Pro for 120 hours, and Enterprise for 360 hours. Outside that window, you'd need to redeploy instead of rolling back.
- **Volume data after leaving a paid plan:** Data is deleted 30 days after expiry on Free/Trial, 60 days after cancellation on Hobby, and 90 days after cancellation on Pro.

content.content:
**Default retention:** Crunchy Bridge keeps 10 days of backups for each cluster, included in the cluster price. The platform takes a daily base backup and streams WAL every 60 seconds or 16MB, whichever comes first.

**Point-in-time recovery (PITR):** The 10-day window supports PITR. You can restore a fork of your cluster to any minute in that period.

**Extended retention:** You can keep additional daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly backups from the Backups tab. These backups cannot be used for PITR, because only the WAL needed to restore to each backup's completion time is kept. A cluster can't be suspended while extended retention is configured.

**After cluster destruction:** Backups are deleted 5 days after you destroy the cluster.

content.content: # Introduction to backups Amazon RDS creates and saves automated backups of your DB instance or Multi-AZ DB cluster during the backup window of your DB instance. RDS creates a storage volume snapshot of your DB instance, backing up the entire DB instance and not just individual databases. RDS saves the automated backups of your DB instance according to the backup retention period that you specify. If necessary, you can recover your DB instance to any point in time during the backup retention period. Automated backups follow these rules: + Your DB instance must be in the `available` state for automated backups to occur. Automated backups don't occur while your DB instance is in a state other than `available`, for example, `storage_full`. + Automated backups don't occur while a DB snapshot copy is running in the same AWS Region for the same database. You can also back up your DB instance manually by creating a DB snapshot. For more information about manually creating a DB snapshot, see [Creating a DB snapshot for a Single-AZ DB instance for Amazon RDS](USER_CreateSnapshot.md). Snapshot and backup functionality supports multi-volume configurations. All backup operations include both the primary volume and any additional storage volumes. Snapshots capture the entire database storage configuration. Point-in-time recovery (PITR) works across all storage volumes. The first snapshot of a DB instance contains the data for the full database. Subsequent snapshots of the same database are incremental, which means that only the data that has changed after your most recent snapshot is saved. You can copy both automatic and manual DB snapshots, and share manual DB snapshots. For more information about copying a DB snapshot, see [Copying a DB snapshot for Amazon RDS](USER_CopySnapshot.md). For more information about sharing a DB snapshot, see [Sharing a DB snapshot for Amazon RDS](USER_ShareSnapshot.md). ## Backup storage Your Amazon RDS backup storage for each AWS Region is composed of the automated backups and manual DB snapshots for that Region. Total backup storage space equals the sum of the storage for all backups in that Region. Moving a DB snapshot to another Region increases the backup storage in the destination Region. Backups are stored in Amazon S3. For more information about backup storage costs, see [Amazon RDS pricing](https://aws.amazon.com/rds/pricing/). If you choose to retain automated backups when you delete a DB instance, the automated backups are saved for the full retention period. If you don't choose **Retain automated backups** when you delete a DB instance, all automated backups are deleted with the DB instance. However, DB snapshots (both final and manual) are independent of automated backups and are not affected by this deletion. If you choose to have Amazon RDS create a final DB snapshot before it deletes your DB instance, you can use that to recover your DB instance. Optionally, you can use a previously created manual snapshot. Manual snapshots are not deleted when an instance is deleted. You can have up to 100 manual snapshots per Region.
